card: Adds an auto_outbound_mode feature to the functional test framework and introduces functional test coverage for outbound connection management. Functional tests typically rely on the test runner explicitly initiating outbound connections, leaving the node's autonomous connection decisions untested end-to-end. By intercepting automatic addrman-driven outbound connections through a local SOCKS5 proxy and redirecting them to controllable Python peers, this test covers stale-tip extra connections, periodic extra block-relay-only connections, and network diversification evictions. It also deduplicates proxy redirection logic in p2p_private_broadcast.py.
changed_since_previous: No substantial architectural or functional changes; diff was rebased onto current master.
evidence: Adds integration test coverage for several previously uncovered outbound connection management features merged over the years: extra full outbound connections due to a stale tip (#11560), periodic block-relay-only connections (#19858), and full outbound connection network diversification (#27213).
Deduplicates 100+ lines of custom SOCKS5 connection interception logic in `p2p_private_broadcast.py` (introduced in #29415) into reusable framework methods.
problem: P2P connection management logic where the node autonomously decides to open and evict outbound connections lacks functional test coverage. Functional tests usually rely on inbound connections or test-initiated outbound connections (`add_outbound_p2p_connection`), leaving behaviors like stale-tip extra outbound connections, periodic block-relay-only feeler connections, and network-diversification eviction rules without end-to-end integration tests.

risk.why: Only alters Python functional test framework code and adds new tests; production node behavior is untouched.

scope_notes: Only touches Python functional tests and test framework utilities (`test/functional/`).
summary: Adds an `auto_outbound_mode` feature to the Python test framework and adds a new test `p2p_outbound_management.py`. In this mode, a node's automatic addrman-driven outbound connections are routed via a SOCKS5 proxy to controllable test framework listeners. The change also refactors `p2p_private_broadcast.py` to use the shared framework implementation instead of its own custom proxy redirection logic.
